h2: A Calendar Answers When, Never What For
lede: A moon phase tracker is the least mystical app in this library and possibly the most useful, because it solves a problem that every practitioner actually has and that almost nobody writes down: knowing which night a working goes on. The arithmetic is the product. The judgement about what belongs on that night is yours, and no amount of phase data will make it for you. Below is the eight-phase framework, the tracking practice that makes it more than a widget, and the two questions worth asking before you time anything by the moon.

sections.h3: The eight phases, and what each one is not
p: Phase attributions in popular practice are usually a list of adjectives, and they are the least useful part of the material. [Moon phases explained, with dates](moon-phases-explained-dates-energies-rituals) and [the eight phases worked through](moon-phases-meaning-8-phases-explained) are the two references that stay operational, because both describe what the geometry does rather than what it feels like.

The one distinction worth learning properly is new against full. [New moon against full moon](new-moon-vs-full-moon-ritual-guide) makes it, and the practical consequence is that beginnings and endings are not the same activity and the popular pairing of both with intention-setting is a category error that costs people a working. [The dark moon, without the scare](the-dark-moon-isnt-scary-a-witchs-perspective) covers the phase most calendars omit.

sections.h3: Timing a spell, which is the actual use
p: The framing that makes the app worth owning: the moon's position selects a window, the aim decides what happens inside it, and doing the aim without the window is usually better than doing the window without the aim. [Moon phase calculator for spells](moon-phase-calculator-for-spells) is the shortest statement of that, and [phases and spell timing](moon-phases-spell-timing-guide) is the longer one with the calendar maths set out.

[Moon phase magic, as a complete guide](lunar-phase-magic-guide) and [the full ritual and spell set](lunar-magic-rituals-spells-complete-guide) are the reference layers. [Moon phase generator, and using cycles for timing](moon-phase-generator-magic-guide) covers the planning view, and [tracking spells across a lunar year](lunar-phase-year-tracking-guide) is what a twelve-month version of this looks like in practice.

sections.h3: What tracking for a year actually changes
p: The interesting finding in the long-run writing is not about the moon. It is that a year of dated records turns an intuition into a reference. [Moon magic for a year](moon-magic-for-a-year-tracking-every-phase) is the honest version, and [a witch's year with a phase app](a-witchs-year-with-the-lunar-phase-app) is the field report from the other side of the same habit. [I followed the moon for a year](lunar-phase-year-test) is the closest thing here to a results write-up, and it is careful not to claim more than the record supports.

The calendar side has its own short literature. [Best lunar calendar apps](best-lunar-calendar-apps-2026) and [best moon phase journals](best-moon-phase-journal-apps-2026) cover the tooling comparison, and [the calculator's own review](lunar-phase-calculator-app-review) with [its methods and accuracy](lunar-phase-calculator-guide-methods-2026) is where you should look before trusting the numbers. [A dated new moon reference](new-moon-dates-2026-2027-ritual-calendar) and [full moon charging nights](full-moon-charging-nights-2026) are the two pages to bookmark.

sections.h3: Eclipses, and the seasons around them
p: Eclipses get their own status in the popular literature and the justification is weak, but the practice of treating the surrounding weeks as a distinct period is defensible on simpler grounds: the calendar is a real boundary and boundaries help you schedule. [Lunar eclipse rituals for 2026](lunar-eclipse-rituals-2026) collects them, and [a single eclipse procedure, step by step](lunar-eclipse-ritual) is the one to read if you want a procedure rather than a list.

[Eclipse season and projection opportunities](eclipse-season-astral-projection-opportunities) makes the cross-reference into dream work, and [moon gazing as a practice](moon-gazing-meditation-practice-guide) is the version that needs no apparatus at all. If your interest is in the moon as a document rather than a schedule, [moon sign astrology](moon-sign-astrology-guide) and [moon sign as emotional blueprint](moon-sign-meaning-emotions-astrology) are the two reference pages, and they cover a completely different question from the one this app answers.

sections.h3: The correspondence layer, and where to stop adding it
p: [Lunar and planetary magic](lunar-and-planetary-magic-moon-magic-rituals-guide) and [its longer treatment](lunar-and-planetary-magic-moon-magic-rituals-guide-3) add planets to the phase, and [practical planetary magic](aikendu-moon-magic-rituals) works a full week frame from a different tradition. The additions are worth learning one at a time. The failure mode is a practice where the correspondence table has become more elaborate than the aim, and the detector for that is simple: if you could not say in one sentence what the working is for, the table is carrying it.

Two articles on the same set from the astrology side keep the layer honest, [the big three](big-three-explained) and [sun, moon and ascendant](sun-moon-ascendant-meaning), because they show that a moon sign is a property of a birth chart rather than of a date. [The moon as a manifestation calendar](the-moon-as-your-manifestation-calendar) is the most common modern use and the one most likely to produce a good month and no working.

sections.h3: Time itself, when the moon is not the point
p: A lunar calendar is a scheduling tool, and scheduling tools get pointed at time itself more often than they should. [What a construct can actually control about time](fotamecus-time-what-a-construct-can-actually-control) and [what an acceleration servitor actually changes](fastar-acceleration-servitor-accuracy-cost) both reach the same conclusion from opposite directions, and both are worth reading before you build anything aimed at a deadline. [Time and causality](time-and-causality-time-magic-ritual-guide-2) is the broader treatment of the question.

The dream-work crossover is [lunar dream incubation before sleep](lunar-dream-incubation-before-sleep-guide), which uses the same calendar to place a question rather than a working. [AIKENDÚ](aikendu-moon-magic-rituals) closes the set with a frame that fits a year rather than a night. If you want the free-versus-paid question answered narrowly, [free lunar phase against the app](free-lunar-phase-vs-lunar-phase-calculator-app) and [the free calculator guide](free-lunar-phase-calculator-guide) are the two pages, and the general version is [free tools against premium apps](free-tools-vs-premium-apps-occult).

foot: The phase gives you a night. The aim gives you the working. If you have only one of the two, you have half a practice, and the half you have is usually the calendar.
